The angled grips turn the palms slightly in from full supination.
Two dumbbells, palms up, curled together (as photographed).
Arms alternate within the set, so every set works both arms once.
Seated back on an incline bench, arms hanging behind the body; the photo alternates arms.
Upper arms on the preacher pad; an EZ bar in the photo.
Machines differ: one bar for both hands, or independent handles that allow one arm.
Straight bar on a low pulley (as photographed).
One arm, facing away from a low pulley with the arm drawn behind the body.
Chest on an incline bench, arms hanging straight down; a bar in the photo.

Two dumbbells, palms facing in, curled together (as photographed).
Palms facing in, each dumbbell curled across the body; arms alternate within the set (as photographed).
Rope on a low pulley, both hands, palms facing in.
Barbell, palms down (as photographed). The wrist is held straight, not curled.
Curled up palms up, turned palms down at the top, lowered palms down; two dumbbells together (as photographed). The grip changes within each rep, which the grip vocabulary has no single word for.
Bar kept against the body as the elbows travel back.

Read as a body-weight curl from an underhand bar grip: the catalog gives no set-up beyond the name, and it is scored on reps like a chin-up. The hands hold body weight, so straps can be used and are not recorded.
Straight bar on a low pulley (as photographed).
Rope on a low pulley, palms facing in (as photographed).
Back on an incline with the cable behind; the catalog does not say one handle or two.
Standing between two high pulleys, both arms (as photographed).
One handle, the working elbow braced.
Chest on an incline bench facing a low pulley, a bar in both hands.
One handle curled across the body, palm facing in; the catalog tags the brachialis and forearms as its main movers, as for a hammer curl.
Barbell, kneeling, forearms on a flat bench, palms up, wrists over the edge (as photographed).
Barbell, kneeling, forearms on a flat bench, palms down, wrists over the edge (as photographed).
Standing, arms held out in front, palms down, winding the cord up and back down (as photographed). Which way the roller is turned is not recorded.
Palms down, arms held out in front, winding the cord up by rolling the top of the roller toward you: each wrist bends back (extends) to wind, then the weight is lowered the same way.
Palms down, arms held out in front, winding the cord up by rolling the top of the roller away from you: each wrist curls down (flexes) to wind, then the weight is lowered the same way.
Palms down against a low pulley; the catalog does not say bar or single handle, or whether the forearm is supported.
Seated, forearm along the thigh, palm up, wrist past the knee (as photographed).
Seated, forearm along the thigh, palm down, wrist past the knee (as photographed).
Standing, arm straight at the side, holding the unloaded end of a dumbbell handle or hammer with the weight in front; the wrist tilts the weight up toward the thumb side.
Standing, arm straight at the side, holding the unloaded end of a dumbbell handle or hammer with the weight behind; the wrist tilts the weight up toward the pinky side.
Seated, forearm supported on the thigh or a bench with the elbow bent to about 90 degrees, holding a handle loaded at one end (or a hammer); the forearm turns palm-down against the load's leverage.
As Lever Pronation, turning palm-up. The elbow angle is part of the definition: with the elbow bent the biceps helps supinate, so the same exercise with a straight arm is a different task.

Seated, forearms on the thighs, palms up; the bar rolls down to the fingertips and is curled back into the palm (as photographed). The fingers must move: a bar held still is a wrist curl or a hold, not this.
A torsion-spring hand gripper closed fully and opened again, one hand at a time.
A hand gripper squeezed shut and held closed, one hand at a time.
A band around the fingertips; the fingers straighten and open against it. A wide band also spreads the fingers, which the hand's own muscles do; that part is not credited to the forearm.
A band anchored over the thumb tip; the tip of the thumb bends against it, so the thumb's end joint must move.
A band over the back of the thumb; the thumb straightens against it at its knuckle and tip.
A band around the thumb and fingers; the thumb moves away from the index finger in the plane of the palm.
Two smooth plates pinched together between fingers and thumb, one hand, at the side (as photographed).
Hanging from a bar with both hands, palms forward; body weight unless assisted or loaded.
Hanging from two towels looped over a bar, gripped in the fists.
An implement in each hand, standing still.
An implement in each hand, walking (as photographed). Time is recorded; distance is not.
One dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand, walking upright. Time is recorded; distance is not.
A barbell held in the crook of both elbows while walking; the hands do not hold the bar, so there is no grip.
Hanging from a bar, palms forward; the set is counted in leg raises, and the grip holds the body throughout.
Hanging from a bar, palms forward; the set is counted in knee raises, and the grip holds the body throughout.
Hanging from a bar, palms forward; the grip holds the body throughout.

Pullover: straight-arm shoulder extension; the attachment and grip vary and are not defined.
Pullover machines load the upper arm through pads; the hands may barely grip.
Pullover: the hands cup one end of the dumbbell rather than gripping a handle, and the grip demand depends on that set-up.
